subject: Renewal pricing: conditional price-latch & bridging credit
messages:
From: Samir Patel <samir@clearforge.ai>
To: irene.choi@redwood.inference.com
Cc: Emma Liu <emma.liu@clearforge.ai>, Procurement <po@clearforge.ai>
Date: Wed, 29 Aug 2028 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Renewal pricing for ClearForge — urgent

Hi Irene,

We’re coming up on our August 31 renewal and usage over the last quarter has exceeded our committed tier by ~60%. We’re evaluating options — ClearForge is committed to scaling with Redwood, but the step-up in list rates for the next term puts a meaningful hit on our forecast.

Can Redwood provide any path to smooth renewal pricing? Specifically: a short-term price hold for 90 days while we finalize capacity planning, and a bridging credit to offset the overage for Q3 usage so procurement can approve the PO.

We’d like to get the terms locked this week if possible. Attaching our current renewal worksheet (see PO request in procurement thread).

Thanks,
Samir
Samir Patel
Head of Platform — ClearForge
attachments: Renewal_Worksheet_Q3.xlsx (spreadsheet)

From: irene.choi@redwood.inference.com
To: Samir Patel <samir@clearforge.ai>
Cc: marissa.cole@redwood.inference.com, david.kim@redwood.inference.com
Date: Wed, 29 Aug 2028 11:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Renewal pricing for ClearForge — urgent

Samir — thanks for the note and context. We want to keep ClearForge as a strategic customer and avoid churn risk given your growth.

Proposed immediate path (subject to approvals):
- 90-day conditional price-latch: hold current blended rate for 90 days from renewal effective date while you finalize capacity plan.
- One-time bridging credit to offset Q3 overage (applied as credit toward invoice at renewal). We’d need to agree on the credit quantum — proposal attached.

I’m looping in Marissa (Account Lead) and David (Finance) to size the bridging credit and confirm margin impact. Can you confirm the total token estimate for the overage window (or confirm Samir’s worksheet is final)? If procurement needs a PO this week, we can prepare a short amendment + PO template for signatures.

Best,
Irene Choi
Director, Commercial Ops — Redwood Inference
attachments: Draft_Amendment_v1.pdf (stub)

From: Emma Liu <emma.liu@clearforge.ai>
To: irene.choi@redwood.inference.com
Cc: Samir Patel <samir@clearforge.ai>, Procurement <po@clearforge.ai>, Legal <contracts@clearforge.ai>
Date: Thu, 30 Aug 2028 08:24:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Renewal pricing for ClearForge — urgent

Irene — thanks, this is helpful. A few clarifications from our side:
- We can accept a 90-day price-hold if there’s a clear trigger at the end of the 90 days (either a capacity-based uplift or reverted rates). We’d prefer a soft cap on unit price rather than a full reversion to list.
- For the bridging credit, procurement needs the dollar amount and whether it is refundable or applied toward future invoices.
- Legal asked that any amendment include a clear definition of what constitutes "usage" (billing units / embeddings vs. chat tokens) to avoid disputes.

We attached a PO template — if you can send a redline of the amendment and the credit schedule, we’ll route internally.

Emma
Procurement Manager — ClearForge
attachments: PO_Template.docx (stub)

From: irene.choi@redwood.inference.com
To: david.kim@redwood.inference.com, marissa.cole@redwood.inference.com
Cc: Samir Patel <samir@clearforge.ai>
Date: Mon, 04 Sep 2028 10:18:00 -07:00
Subject: Internal: Approval request — ClearForge bridging credit and 90-day price-latch

Team,

Summary: ClearForge is requesting (A) 90-day conditional price-latch, and (B) bridging credit to offset Q3 overage so they can issue PO. They’re strategic and scaled quickly; retention is high priority.

I recommend the following conservative structure:
- Price-latch: hold effective blended rate for 90 days, with an agreed post-latch uplift band capped at +8% (i.e., soft cap).
- Bridging credit: one-time credit equal to 40% of the incremental cost above their committed tier for Q3 (applied as account credit against renewal invoice).
- Credit expires if invoice not executed within 45 days of amendment signing.

Requested: David — approve the credit amount up to $120k (worst-case) and confirm accounting treatment. Marissa — ok to present to the customer if finance signs off? I’ve attached a Draft_Amendment_v2 and a Bridging_Credit_Schedule.

Thanks,
Irene
attachments: Draft_Amendment_v2.pdf, Bridging_Credit_Schedule.xlsx

From: david.kim@redwood.inference.com
To: irene.choi@redwood.inference.com, marissa.cole@redwood.inference.com
Cc: Samir Patel <samir@clearforge.ai>
Date: Tue, 05 Sep 2028 09:06:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Internal: Approval request — ClearForge bridging credit and 90-day price-latch

Irene — reviewed. Approve structure with the following guardrails:
- Approve up to $110,000 bridging credit (not to exceed $110k). If expected credit exceeds that, we need a layered approval (Finance Director + RevOps).
- Apply credit as non-refundable account credit to be used against the renewal invoice only.
- Accounting: recognize as contra-revenue spread across remaining contract term; coordinate with bookkeeping on FY/Q3 close.

Marissa — you can present the amended terms as long as we cap at $110k. If ClearForge insists on higher credit, escalate and I’ll fast-track the extra approval.

David
Director, Finance Operations — Redwood Inference

From: irene.choi@redwood.inference.com
To: Samir Patel <samir@clearforge.ai>, Emma Liu <emma.liu@clearforge.ai>, Procurement <po@clearforge.ai>
Cc: marissa.cole@redwood.inference.com, david.kim@redwood.inference.com
Date: Mon, 18 Sep 2028 16:42:00 -07:00
Subject: RE: Renewal pricing for ClearForge — confirmation of amended terms and next steps

Samir / Emma — thanks for the patience. Quick recap of what we can offer and next steps: 

Offer: 
- 90-day conditional price-latch: maintain your current blended billing rates for 90 days from the renewal effective date. After 90 days, either (a) rates move to agreed post-latch band (<= +8%), or (b) we revert to standard list if no capacity agreement in place.
- Bridging credit: one-time non-refundable credit, equal to up to $110,000 (40% of incremental cost above committed tier as discussed). Credit will be applied against the renewal invoice.
- Definition of usage: amendment includes explicit billing unit definitions (chat tokens and embedding units) — please review Draft_Amendment_v2.

Next steps: 
1) Emma/Procurement: confirm acceptance of the $110k cap and sign the attached amendment + PO_Template.docx.
2) Once signed, finance will apply the credit to the renewal invoice and we’ll schedule a 30-day checkpoint to review capacity plans.

Attached: Draft_Amendment_v2.pdf, Bridging_Credit_Schedule.xlsx, PO_Template.docx

If that looks acceptable, can Procurement return a signed PO by EOD Wednesday so we can lock the renewal effective date?

Best,
Irene Choi
Director, Commercial Ops — Redwood Inference
attachments: Draft_Amendment_v2.pdf, Bridging_Credit_Schedule.xlsx, PO_Template.docx
